text: We accepted the draft, though the timetable left delegations scant opportunity to scrutinize or refine it.
We supported adoption. Our criticism was that the penholder brought the text to a decision before delegations had a meaningful chance to revise it.
We could vote in favour and still object that delegations were given an unreasonably short window to agree on the wording.
The text could have been clearer, and we regretted that too little time had been provided for delegates to work through it.
Some called the negotiations rushed, but we believed enough time had been allowed. We focused on the clarity of the text.
We recorded another delegation's claim of rushed negotiations without endorsing its assessment. Our own position concerns monitoring.
The next negotiation should move quickly. We take no position on whether the time allowed for this draft was too short.
We voted in favour, though the resolution is difficult to interpret. We make no claim about the length of the negotiations.
We called for speedy action once the text was adopted. The pace of implementing the reform matters for peacebuilding.
We supported voluntary funding aligned with national priorities and asked that the authority of the Fund manager be stated clearly.
The penholder's short timetable was appropriate. Negotiations moved quickly and we had enough time to agree the wording.
